title: CWE-639: Authorization bypass through a user-controlled key
prerequisites: an endpoint that accepts a key from the caller — an id, a path segment or a body field — and uses it to select which record to act on
at least two principals whose objects the same endpoint can reach, so a swapped key crosses an ownership boundary
excerpt: The weakness sits between authentication and authorization: the endpoint checks who the caller is, then trusts a key the caller supplied to pick which object to serve or mutate, without checking that the caller is allowed to reach that particular object. A single account can never show this — the key always resolves to something that account already owns. The demonstrated effect is a second principal's object read, changed or deleted through the first principal's session, not merely that an unfamiliar key value was accepted without an error.
